prompt:
Original Taiwanese game art for "Tainan Gazetteer" (府城夜巡地圖), set in Tainan around 1930.
Style: handmade layered paper sculpture (紙雕 / kirie), the same for buildings, trees, plants,
fences, ground tiles, icons and props. Every shape is a piece of cut paper: visible paper fibres,
slightly soft hand-cut edges, pieces overlapping in shallow layers with small soft contact shadows
where one sheet sits on another. Colour is printed on the paper: clearly visible risograph /
stencil print grain and uneven ink density across every flat area, never a clean digital fill.
Weathering is welcome: irregular faded patches, not neat squares.
Details are built from few, large cut pieces (roof tiles, bricks, window frames, leaves, petals,
stones, planks), not painted lines and not crowded tiny patterns. Plants are natural and
asymmetric.
Colour: follow the real object, then mute it: pale, slightly greyed, warm. Typical tones: warm
cream, pale brick red, coral, sage and grey-green, mustard, indigo, wood brown, stone grey.
No saturated red-against-green contrast.
Buildings: strictly frontal elevation, no perspective, three or four flat paper layers.
Do NOT make: a 3D render or clay/plastic model, smooth bevelled relief, realistic or painterly
illustration, photo textures, thick foam layers, glow, glossy highlights, black outline strokes,
smooth gradients, depth of field.
Output: generated natively on a fully TRANSPARENT background (real alpha including enclosed
holes, no backdrop, no glow, no chroma-key colour, no coloured fringe), every object complete
and separated by clear transparent gutters, no ground, no base, no cast shadow outside the
object, no text, no captions, no logos.

A single standalone Delonix regia flame tree cut-paper game sprite. Keep the centered tree comfortably inset and never enlarge to fill the frame: aim for tree silhouette 1110 px wide by 770 px high inside a 1536 × 1024 landscape canvas, with visible clear padding equivalent to roughly 1/7 of the canvas height at both top and bottom. Same asset scale as approved plumeria. An original asymmetrical, spreading low umbrella form with several rounded sage-green compound-foliage pads and a warm gray-brown multi-fork trunk of tapered angular paper segments, broad exposed branch openings and intentionally uneven reach. The flower accents should be tiny relative to the tree: about five percent of its height, each 30–48 px wide, with about fifty muted terracotta and coral tiny five-petal cutouts scattered naturally, leaving the sage green leafy pads as the dominant shape. Equivalently fit roughly thirty individual flower diameters across its wide canopy. A few visible small feathery leaf sprays in each mass, each paper leaf element approximately 36–54 pixels. Preserve the fine warm paper fibers and dense uneven ink grain. Plumeria input guides physical element scale and paper cutouts only, paper atlas cherry and maple guide trunk and silhouette layer treatment, and old flame tree is an example of the general species silhouette but its flowers are overlarge. No ground, backdrop or haze, clean native alpha.
notes: 使用內建 image_gen 原生透明模式。flameTree.png 取自 candidate-4.png，保留原始像素與 alpha。畫布 1536 × 1024 px，樹身實測約 743 px 高（alpha > 127），比 780 px 目標小約 5%。一般 alpha 合成預覽未見光暈。實景參考：NParks 鳳凰木物種頁 https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/2/8/2838 （傘形樹冠、二回羽狀複葉與橘紅花）；NParks 實樹照片 https://www.nparks.gov.sg/publications-resources/articles/singapore-s-international-trees （橫展枝幹及花色）。保留全部四張原始候選圖。

Generate one standalone game sprite of a mature Taiwanese flame tree, 鳳凰木 (Delonix regia), single asset. Generate directly at the intended pixel scale, with an approximately 780-pixel-tall tree silhouette from root to crown (130 game units at 6×). Prefer a landscape canvas with room for the broad tree, modest clear transparent margins, and the entire silhouette intact. Do not shrink the tree to fit a sprite sheet.

Image 1, approved plumeria: reference the scale of the individual leaves and flowers, tactile paper technique and stepped angular changes in trunk width. Use its tree artwork only; do not reproduce the halo shown in the preview. Image 2, approved paper atlas: reference the bottom row's cherry and maple trees for overlapping cut-paper, exposed sharply kinked trunks, paper fibers and grain. Image 3, current flame tree: subject reference only, with an umbrella crown and transverse branches; replace the oversize floral masses with many small, individually legible orange-red blossoms scattered irregularly over the pale green paper canopy, each 30–48 px across. Keep green dominant and leave green space between blossoms. Model the five petals of real Delonix with slightly unequal shapes and occasional subtle lighter markings. Individual small feathery compound leaf pieces are approximately 36–54 px long, suggested along the contours and overlaps of a few large rounded sage-green paper canopy sections. A warm gray-brown trunk with successive angular, tapering segments opens into unequal laterally extended branches. Uneven, naturally asymmetric umbrella silhouette, branch gaps at varying heights. Muted warm terracotta and faded coral blossoms. Crisp isolated silhouette, physically cut paper contours and only internal paper contact shadows. The canvas beyond the tree and all gaps between branches must be alpha zero. No glow or haze anywhere.

Single isolated sprite, natural mature Delonix regia, Taiwanese flame tree. A low spreading off-center umbrella crown, stepped angular gray-brown paper trunk and long lateral branches with clear transparent openings. A few overlapping rounded muted sage-green masses of bipinnate foliage. Each compound leaf paper detail is 36–54 pixels long. The crown is generously peppered with roughly forty small, discrete muted orange-red five-petal flowers, about 35 pixels across on average; at the final drawing scale a flower is approximately one twenty-second of the tree's height and one thirty-fifth of its width. Keep a clear green interval between flowers. Draw the artwork at 6 pixels per game unit: the complete tree from trunk base to tallest tip occupies about 780 pixels of height, and no more than 1,250 pixels of width. Center within a 1536×1024 RGBA canvas, with about 120 pixels of empty transparent margin on every side. The tree should occupy the middle three quarters of the canvas height, with no ground or additional scene elements. Native transparency, with sharply defined cutout boundaries, fully transparent gaps, no halo. Reference 1 (plumeria) for angular trunk and the physical scale of flowers and leaves; reference 2 (atlas) for the handmade layered paper, soft fibers, printed grains and angular tree structure of the cherry and maple; reference 3 (old flame tree) for the species and overall wide canopy only.
